podcast.body: This "glambop" song was the lead single from the 'Aladdin Sane' album. It topped out at number 71 on the Hot 100, indicating it wasn't a big US pop hit, but the strength of Bowie's potent persona at the time ensured the album itself still sold well regardless of the single's chart performance. "Though Aladdin's scene's lead single, The Glambop Jean-Geney, wasn't a big US pop hit, topping out at number 71 on the Hot 100, the David Bowie persona was now so potent, his album sold well regardless."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.body: This song from the "Aladdin Sane" album was written in part about his friend Iggy Pop and inspired by Jean Genet, a writer, poet, and political activist. The track captured the essence of Bowie's transitional "Aladdin Sane" persona, which took the Ziggy Stardust concept to a new level. "The Gene Genie written in part about his even crazier friend, Eiki Pop, and inspired by Jean Genie. Another friend who was a writer, poet, and political activist."
